unnormalised_note: mu, nu are raw exp(marginal_logp), NOT renormalised on U(x), per spec.

numerical_feasibility.note: At reg=1e-2 (the pre-reg's specified entropic regulariser), the Sinkhorn solver (both plain and log-domain-stabilised variants were tried) fails to converge for the large majority of target-steps. Diagnosed directly, not guessed: within a SINGLE target, the before- and after-model's own raw (unnormalised) total probability mass on that target's U(x) can differ by ~10+ orders of magnitude (checked on a real example: mu in [1.2e-20, 3.7e-11], nu in [1.8e-10, 1.0] for the SAME target/recipe set) -- a genuine property of the data (how much raw mass each model's marginal estimator places on this small recipe set), not a scale artifact a global rescaling can fix (KL(k*p||k*q) = k*KL(p||q) only rescales a SHARED constant k applied to both mu and nu together; it cannot correct an asymmetry BETWEEN mu and nu themselves). The T values for the handful of target-steps that do converge are reported below for completeness, but are NOT treated as a reliable sample -- they are almost certainly the numerically easiest (most scale-balanced) targets, not a representative draw, so the prediction (median T higher for S2-S4 than S5-S7) is reported as NOT TESTABLE AS SPECIFIED, not as a null or a pass/fail. Resolving this would mean departing from the pre-reg's literal reg=1e-2 (e.g. a larger regulariser, which changes the OT solution itself) -- a decision not made unilaterally here.
